header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 20:00 UTC
Duration: 1h12m (72 minutes)
Attendees: Lena Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (BlueArc SE Enablement), Priya Menon (BlueArc SE Manager), Kai Robertson (BlueArc Product)
Recording: fireflies.ai/export/2025-02-14-pivot-prove
summary: Internal enablement: rapid demo practice focusing on pivots for price/latency objections and sharpening competitive messaging vs Anthropic/OpenAI/self-hosted options. Four 8-minute roleplay rounds with peer feedback and prioritized action items.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: ok everyone welcome, um this is the pivot and prove, uh hyperfocus sparring session, we'll do short rounds and quick feedback. we'll aim for 8 minutes per round, clock's up, move on.
[00:15] Marco: mm-hmm. quick note - we're trying to harden the opening, and the 'why Redwood' hooks at 30-60s. focus on production economics - latency, cost and reliability.
[00:35] Jordan: sounds good, and just so you know, our reps get the latency question a lot - they say "your numbers are great but our infra folks worry about on-prem" so we want good VPC/on-prem language.
[00:50] Ava: right. we'll practice the VPC pivot and the dedicated capacity tradeoff. also, there will be some mistranscriptions in the notes so don't assume perfect wording. (laughs)
[01:05] Priya: thanks. one ask - can you show a quick quip on fallback behavior? like when a model gets slow how Redwood keeps UX stable.
[01:20] Marco: sure, I'll demo routing and fallback: policy based routing to cheaper model variants, automatic fallback to hosted replicas, and KV cache to reduce repeat token cost. note - sometimes this is transcribed as K V cash or K V cache — just clarifying.
[01:40] Roleplay Round 1 - Jordan as buyer, Lena as AE
[01:45] Jordan: thanks Lena, we're exploring LLM infra. key concerns: latency spikes, data residency, and total TCO.
[01:55] Lena: absolutely, appreciate that. at a high level Redwood is about predictable per-token economics and consistent latency across hosted and private deployments. for latency spikes we use routing + pre-warmed pools — so you can set SLOs and automatic fallback.
[02:15] Jordan: what about private? our security team insists on VPC and KMS.
[02:20] Lena: a great question. we have Redwood Private - it gives you a customer-managed control plane, KMS integrations for key management, and audit logs. for on-prem we also have an air-gapped package though that's usually reserved for regulated customers.
[02:40] Jordan: ok cost - your public numbers look good but our CFO wants to know if quantized models will affect quality.
[02:48] Lena: we recommend quantization profiles per workload; Redwood Optimize provides recommendations and quality monitoring with evals to track regressions. in practice, you see 2-4x cost reduction for embedded-like workloads with minimal quality hit, but we always gate with eval sets.
[03:10] Jordan: hmm ok.
[03:15] Feedback: Marco: good opener but call out an explicit success metric early - e.g., "we'll get 99th percentile under X ms". Ava: add a 15s 'fallback story' before going deep.
[03:40] Round 2 - Price/Latency pushback - Priya as buyer, Marco as SE
[03:45] Priya: we heard you, but our architect says to self-host to avoid vendor lock and manage GPUs.
[03:52] Marco: totally fair. two quick points — one, rein in the economics: Redwood's unified runtime often reduces infra spend through batching, KV caching, and model routing; second, operations overhead: we provide a managed control plane for hosted/dedicated and a private option that maps closely to your network, reducing build time.
[04:20] Priya: and for disaster scenarios?
[04:24] Marco: we support cross-region failover and can set canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant so UX stays up. (brief pause) sometimes that line comes out clunky, rephrase to "canary + automatic fallback keeps your app responsive during incidents."
[04:48] Jordan: competitor question - how do you compare to Anthropic and OpenAI?
[04:52] Ava: we position versus OpenAI as lower unit cost for production due to batching and caching, and versus Anthropic we emphasize deployment flexibility (dedicated + private) and observability. (note: keep the competitive phrasing succinct).
[05:10] Marco: also call out our 'rollout policies' and trace hooks in the console when you want to prove fixes to engineering.
[05:28] Feedback: Lena: good. but call out a specific customer story - e.g., "Acme Media reduced per-token cost 37% after enabling prefix caching" - placeholder okay.
[05:45] Round 3 - Rapid pivot drill - Kai as technical buyer, Ava as SE
[05:50] Kai: our priority is reproducible latency under 150ms for 8k context. how does Redwood handle kernel selection?
[05:58] Ava: short answer - runtime picks optimized kernels per model and sequence length, plus continuous batching controls the tail. we can surface performance profiles per model in the catalog.
[06:15] Kai: okay model ops - how much effort for our infra team?
[06:18] Ava: depends on deployment - hosted is zero infra, dedicated is reserved GPUs with ops handoff, private gives you a control plane that maps to your network. for on-prem there is a packaged install. (muttering: sometimes folks mishear "control plane" as "control planee")
[06:38] Feedback: Marco: great deep tech answers. suggest a 20s explainer about quantization types and what they mean for perf vs quality.
[06:55] Round 4 - Objection escalation - Jordan as buyer escalates to procurement
[07:00] Jordan: procurement asked if Redwood supports SSO/SAML and SOC2.
[07:05] Lena: yes - we have SSO, SAML, RBAC, SOC 2 type II and can provide encrypted audit logs with KMS. provide link to security page in follow-up.
[07:20] Jordan: if we go dedicated, do we still get the console and tracing?
[07:25] Lena: yes, dedicated includes console access, per-route metrics, and token-level cost breakdowns. you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts.
[07:40] Feedback: Priya: tighten the procurement language - "we can provide SOC2 artifacts and a security pack during procurement" - short, confident.
[07:55] Breakout quick coaching - coaches swap notes (fast)
[08:00] Marco: tip - when you hear "self-host" question, lead with "what would you need to build to match our per-token economics?" it reframes cost vs engineering spend.
[08:15] Ava: script a 30s rebuttal for on-prem: "if you need air-gap we offer a packaged install with audit logs + KMS; if you want hybrid we can route sensitive traffic to Private and keep other workloads on hosted to balance cost."
[08:40] Lena: ok quick live demo scenario - Marco will run a 3-min console walkthrough focusing on rollouts and traces. cameras off, just narrate.
[08:50] Marco: demo start - opening console, show model catalog, select model variant, show latency/throughput chart, enable canary rollout 10% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback policy; show token cost per route.
[09:30] (transcription noise) Speaker 7: uh uh that last line was recorded as "token cost per root".
[09:40] Jordan: that was clean. suggestion - show a numbered checklist for security buyers: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
[09:55] Roleplay debrief and critique - each gives 1 improvement
[10:00] Priya: call out the timeline to production - e.g., "we can pilot in 4-6 weeks with a small dataset and pre-warmed pool".
[10:20] Marco: add a one-slide microbenchmark showing 95/99p latency and a cost delta vs baseline.
[10:35] Lena: closing - great energy. everyone met the time box. we'll incorporate the script edits and post the demo clip examples.
[10:48] Jordan: thanks - we'll pull persona notes and loss reasons and share with you by Wednesday.
[11:00] Recap (verbal): Lena: action items - I will annotate the script, Marco makes the clip, Ava updates battlecard, Jordan shares buyer persona + loss reasons. follow-up practice scheduled.
[11:20] Short misc chatter and sign-off (some crosstalk)
[11:35] Marco: one last note - during live deals use the 'fallback story' early; it calms procurement and infra.
[11:50] Lena: perfect. thanks everyone, session ends.
[12:00] (meeting end)

Notes: transcript contains intentional small transcription errors and shorthand; references to product names sometimes truncated (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwood dedicate"), and technical terms occasionally mis-typed in auto transcript. Links referenced during call: security pack (drive link placeholder), internal demo clips (gdrive/clip1), annotated script (drive link).
